label: live

steps.assertion: The Pro project terminal opens in its registered dedicated checkout.
The dev-madrid device terminal uses the existing relay and prints the actual remote hostname.
Type or dictate a command and Run send echo hello through the real PTY.
Sticky Ctrl and C interrupt sleep within two seconds and preserve its non-zero exit record.
Reload reconnects the same terminal and replays hello in its scrollback.
The copy buttons include exactly the requested command range and strip every escape code.

steps.assertion: Take over in browser attaches a real native thread session; leaving detaches and returns it to Jevellan.
Every captured screen passes the dedicated live vision rubric in this layout.

screens.expected: a connected project terminal with usable controls and no clipped text

cosmetic: Header subtitle host/path is cut off with an ellipsis ('/Users/ggomes...').
The last key in the shortcut row is cut off at the right edge, and nothing shows the row can scroll to reach more keys.
Terminal output breaks words mid-line ('jevellan-l / ive-sandbox', 'jevellan-live- / sandbox %'), which is normal terminal wrapping but harder to read on a narrow screen.
The 'Project' label is centred between 'Connected' and 'Close terminal', and it's unclear whether it is a tab, a badge or a status.

screens.expected: a connected dev-madrid terminal with the remote hostname and usable controls

cosmetic: The special-key row is clipped at the right edge: a partly visible button follows the → key. It looks like a horizontally scrollable row, but nothing shows that it scrolls.
A stray 'hostname' line appears above the first prompt, probably local echo before the prompt was drawn.
There are two hamburger menu buttons stacked in the header (Conversations and Terminal), which is redundant.
A thin black horizontal line near the bottom of the terminal area looks like a stray border or cursor line.

screens.expected: terminal copy and Send to controls reachable at this layout

cosmetic: The header path is truncated ('/Users/ggomes…'), so the full working directory isn't visible.
The first and last buttons in the quick-key row ('→' and '⋯') are partly clipped at the left and right edges. This suggests the row scrolls sideways but gives no clear sign that it does.
The long shell prompt ('ggomes@Goncalos-MacBook-Pro jevellan-live-sandbox %') wraps onto two lines, which makes the terminal output harder to scan.
The 'Copied' confirmation is plain unstyled text below the buttons, so it's easy to miss.

screens.expected: a browser terminal attached to a resumed native coding session, past setup and trust dialogs, with usable exit controls

cosmetic: The header path is cut off ('/home/ggo...'), so the full working directory isn't visible.
The terminal status line is cut off at the right edge ('bypass permissions on (shift+tab to').
The last key in the special-keys row is partly hidden at the right edge. The row looks horizontally scrollable, so the key is probably still reachable.

The terminal shows a stop hook error ('/bin/sh: 1: /Users/ggomes/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.0/bin/node: not found'). This is an environment problem, not a layout problem, but it clutters the session output.
The 'Project' label floats between 'Connected' and 'Close terminal' and doesn't clearly read as a tab or a status.

observations: Usage records come from runtime-reported turn outcomes. Missing tokens or cost remain unknown; minutes include concurrent sessions.
